entries.source:
"Arc Two, mostly," Isa says. "That was where the habitation decks were. Arc One had the good machine shops, but their gravity used to cut out whenever the ore processor started."
She smiles at the memory.
"You learned to keep one hand near a railing and never put a tool down without clipping it to something. The wreck-farms supplied whatever the station couldn't make, and every broken machine became three working machines if you gave the mechanics enough time."
Isa rests the spanner against her shoulder.
"People say a place like that teaches you how to survive. Mostly, it teaches you that almost anything can be repaired if enough people are willing to hold it together."
entries.target:
"主要是第二弧，" 艾薩說道。"那裡是居住甲板所在的位置。第一弧雖然有設備完善的機加工車間，但每當礦石處理器啟動時，那裡的重力就會中斷。"
她回想起這段往事，露出了微笑。
"你學會了一隻手要緊貼欄杆，而且絕不在將工具夾在某處之前就隨意放下。 殘骸農場供應著空間站無法自行製造的一切，只要給機械師們足夠的時間，每一台故障的機器都能變為三台能正常運作的機器。"
艾薩將扳手靠在肩上。
"人們說，那樣的地方會教你如何生存。 但最重要的是，它教會你：只要有足夠多的人願意齊心協力，幾乎任何東西都能被修好。"

"Of course not."
Isa answers too quickly.
"I don't miss the recycler alarms, or the gravity failures, or food that tasted like somebody had described vegetables to a nutrient printer."
She looks past the comm pickup for a moment.
"I miss knowing every voice on the maintenance channel. I miss people shouting repair advice through three decks of open conduit. I miss knowing that if one bulkhead failed, half the Ring would arrive with welding torches before the pressure alarm finished sounding."
Her gaze returns to you.
"It's still home. This fleet is too. Don't make that expression; I'm not saying it twice."
entries.target:
"當然不是。"
艾薩回答得太快了。
"我不會錯過回收器的警報聲、重力系統故障，或是那種彷彿有人向營養素列印機描述蔬菜後印出來的食物。"
她目光越過通訊接收器，凝視片刻。
"我懷念能認出維修頻道上每一個聲音的日子。 我懷念人們透過三層甲板的開放式管線大聲喊出維修建議的樣子。我懷念那種感覺——只要有一道隔艙壁失效，在壓力警報聲尚未停止之前，半個環的成員就會帶著焊接槍趕來。"
她的目光又回到了你身上。
"這裡依然是家。這支艦隊也是。別露出那種表情；我不會說第二遍的。"
entries.backTranslation:
" Of course not. "
Isa answered too quickly.
" I wouldn’t miss the recycler’s alarm, a malfunction in the gravity system, or that food that looks like it was printed by a nutrient printer after someone described vegetables to it. "
Her gaze drifted past the comm receiver and lingered for a moment.
" I miss the days when I could recognize every voice on the maintenance channel. I miss the way people used to shout out repair suggestions through the open conduits spanning three decks. I miss that feeling—wherever a bulkhead failed, half the crew would be rushing over with their welding torches before the pressure alarms had even stopped blaring. "
Her gaze returned to you.
" This is still home. So is this fleet. Don’t give me that look; I won’t say it again. "

entries.source:
Isa exhales.
"Badly? Weirdly?"
She turns her slate over in her hands.
"I spent most of my life wondering if Isaac Leicester was my father. I figured maybe he was some spacer. Engineer, if I was lucky. Maybe somebody who got caught in the Collapse and shoved his kid into the safest cryopod he could find."
She gives a small shrug.
"Turns out he built the hypershunts, built Gan Eden, started a religious revolution, disappeared through a Gate, and spent the rest of his life alone inside a world the size of a solar system."
A pause.
"So I've adjusted my expectations a little."
entries.target:
艾薩嘆了口氣。
"很糟？很奇怪？"
她手裡翻轉著石板。
"我大半輩子都在想，艾薩克·萊斯特是不是我的父親。我猜他或許是個太空人。如果運氣好的話，可能是位工程師。 也許是某個在崩潰中被困住，把孩子塞進他能找到的最安全冷凍艙的人。"
她微微聳了聳肩。
"結果發現，他不僅建造了超空間分流器、建立了伊甸園、發動了一場宗教革命，還透過星門消失無蹤，並在一個大小如太陽系般的世界裡獨自度過餘生。"
她停頓了一下。
"所以我稍微調整了一下我的期望。"
entries.backTranslation:
Isaac sighed.
" Is it bad? Is it strange? "
She turned the stone tablet over in her hands.
" I’ve spent most of my life wondering if Isaac Lester is my father. I guess he might have been an astronaut. If I’m lucky, maybe an engineer. Maybe he was someone trapped in a disaster who shoved his child into the safest cryochamber he could find. "
She shrugged slightly.
"As it turned out, he not only built the hyperspace diverter, founded Eden, and sparked a religious revolution, but also vanished through the Stargate to spend the rest of his life alone on a world the size of a solar system. "
She paused for a moment.
" So I adjusted my expectations slightly. "

entries.source:
"This thing... Ziggurat... I don't like it. Commander, I recommend we isolate the thing. Seal off its display berth." 
Isa rubs her temples. 
"At least until I can figure out where that damn ringing sound is coming from inside it." 
Her rubbing intensifies; her frown deepens.
entries.target:
"這玩意兒……通靈塔……我不喜歡。指揮官，我建議我們將它隔離。封鎖它的展示艙位。"
艾薩揉著太陽穴。
"至少要等到我搞清楚那該死的嗡鳴聲是從它內部哪裡傳來的為止。"
她揉得更用力了；眉頭也皺得更深了。
entries.backTranslation:
" This thing… the Gilgamesh Pyramid… I don’t like it. Commander, I suggest we isolate it. Seal off its display bay. "
Isa massaged her temples.
" At least until I figure out where that damn buzzing sound is coming from inside it. "
She rubbed even harder; her brow furrowed even deeper.

entries.source:
The workshop is silent.
Isa's entire team has gathered beneath the Onslaught Mk.I's projected silhouette. Salvagers who normally argue over stripped bolts stand shoulder to shoulder with yard engineers, all staring upward. The shape is crude and strangely proportioned, but unmistakable.
Isa does not look away when you enter.
"Do you understand what you brought home?" she asks quietly. "The Onslaught. The one every other has spent thousands of cycles trying to remember."
entries.target:
工作坊一片寂靜。
艾薩的整個團隊都聚集在攻勢 Mk.I投影出的輪廓下方。平時總為拆下的螺栓爭執不休的回收者，此刻與船塢工程師並肩而立，所有人皆抬頭凝視。那輪廓雖顯粗糙且比例怪異，卻毫無疑問就是它。
當你走進來時，艾薩 沒有移開視線。
"你明白自己帶回了什麼嗎？"她輕聲問道。 "攻勢號。那艘讓其他人耗費數千個週期仍試圖回想的船。"
entries.backTranslation:
Silence fell over the workshop.
Isa’s entire team had gathered beneath the silhouette projected by the Assault Mk.I. The scavengers, who usually bickered endlessly over dismantled bolts, now stood shoulder to shoulder with the shipyard engineers, all looking up in awe. Though the silhouette was rough and disproportionate, there was no doubt—it was the ship.
When you walked in, Isa didn’t look away.
" Do you realize what you’ve brought back? " she asked softly. " The Assault. The ship that others had spent thousands of cycles trying to recall. "

entries.source:
"We have our own saints." Isa finally lowers her eyes. "I've heard the Mk.I be called a myth. The Domain's navy, its forges, its gates, all hammered into one heroic hammer and sent to fight some impossible enemy in the dark."
She looks back at the ancient hull.
"Then one day the myth drifts out of the abyss."
entries.target:
"我們有自己的聖人。" 艾薩終於垂下了眼簾。"我聽說 Mk.I 被稱為神話。 人之領的海軍、其鍛造坊、其城門，全都熔鑄成一把英雄之錘，被派往黑暗中對抗某個不可能的敵人。"
她回頭望向那艘古老的船體。
"然後某一天，這個神話從深淵中飄了出來。"
entries.backTranslation:
" We have our own saint. " Aisa finally lowered her gaze. " I’ve heard that the Mk.I is called a myth. The Navy of the Land of Men, its forges, and its city gates—all were forged into a single hammer of heroes, sent into the darkness to confront an impossible enemy. "
She looked back at the ancient hull.
" Then one day, this myth drifted out of the abyss. "

entries.source:
"Enough." The reverence in Isa's voice gives way to mounting professional excitement. She unfolds diagrams of the replaceable vambrace armor, the shieldless hull, and the electromechanical automation whispering through every major system.
"The crew kept rebuilding themselves alongside it. Wounded, augmented, replaced, until the people and the ship stopped being separate things. All that remained was a factory serial and one final order repeated across the ages."
A fire-control pattern detaches from the diagrams. You recall what the ship said when you were there.
entries.target:
"夠了。" 艾薩語氣中的敬意逐漸被日益高漲的專業熱情所取代。 她展開了可更換護腕裝甲、無盾艦體，以及貫穿每個主要系統、低語般運轉的電氣機械自動化系統的示意圖。
"船員們始終與之並行重建著自己。 受傷、強化、替換，直到船員與飛船不再是兩件獨立的事物。剩下的只有一個工廠序列號，以及一個跨越時代反覆傳頌的最終指令。"
一個火控圖案從示意圖中脫離出來。 你憶起當初身處那裡時，這艘船曾說過的話。
entries.backTranslation:
" Enough. " The respect in Aisa’s tone was gradually replaced by a growing professional enthusiasm. She unfolded schematics of the interchangeable wrist armor, the unshielded hull, and the electromechanical automation system—whispering as it operated—that ran through every major system.
" The crew was constantly rebuilding themselves in tandem with it. Injured, reinforced, replaced—until the crew and the ship were no longer two separate entities. All that remained was a factory serial number and a final command passed down through the ages. "
A fire-control pattern breaks away from the schematic. You recall the words the ship spoke back when you were there.

Isa stands beneath the Abundant Mercy's projected silhouette, unusually quiet.
"Invictus-patterns we see around these parts are built around deciding who dies," she says. "This one was built around deciding who gets another chance. Every launch rail, every damage-control route, every recovery station. It all points the same way."
entries.target:
艾薩佇立在豐沛慈悲號投影出的剪影之下，異常沉默。
"我們在這片區域所見的不敗模式，其核心在於決定誰該死，" 她說道。 "而這座設施的設計核心，則是決定誰能獲得第二次機會。每條發射軌道、每條損害控制路線、每個救援站，全都指向同一個方向。"
entries.backTranslation:
Aisa stood beneath the silhouette projected by the Abundant Compassion, unusually silent.
" The core of the invincible pattern we’ve observed in this region lies in determining who should die, " she said. " And the core of this facility’s design is determining who gets a second chance. Every launch track, every damage control route, every rescue station—all point in the same direction. "

entries.source:
For once, Isa has no slate in her hands. No schematics, no lists, no half-disassembled parts balanced on the furniture. Just a travel case at her feet and a hard little smile she is trying, unsuccessfully, to hide.
"The Hall can run without me staring over its shoulder now," she says. "Every ledger is clean. Every weird old hull has taught us what it was going to teach from a dock. So if you'll have me, Captain, I want to join you. I want to see what legacies looks like when they're being made."
entries.target:
難得一見，艾薩手中沒有石板。沒有設計圖、沒有清單、也沒有半拆解的零件堆在家具上。 腳邊只有一個旅行箱，以及她試圖隱藏卻未能如願的那抹堅毅而微帶苦澀的笑容。
"現在榮耀大廳已經不需要我時刻在背後監督了，" 她說道。 "每本帳簿都一塵不染。每一艘古怪的老船體，都已在碼頭上將它該傳授的知識教給了我們。所以，船長，如果您願意接納我，我想加入您的行列。 我想親眼見證傳奇在鑄就之際的模樣。"
entries.backTranslation:
It was a rare sight: Aisa wasn’t holding a tablet. There were no blueprints, no lists, and no pile of partially disassembled parts scattered across the furniture. At her feet lay only a suitcase and that determined, slightly bitter smile she’d tried—but failed—to hide.
" The Hall of Glory no longer needs me to be constantly watching over it from behind, " she said. " Every ledger is spotless. Every quirky old hull has already taught us the lessons it was meant to impart at the dock. So, Captain, if you’re willing to accept me, I’d like to join your crew. I want to witness with my own eyes what a legend looks like as it’s being forged. "

Isa does an exaggerated curtsy.
"Ma'am!" she repeats. "Hear that?" She calls over her shoulder, to the genial cheers of her men. "We're respectable citizens now!"
Isa straightens and gives your entourage an appraising look. Her gaze passes over the uniforms, the sidearms, and finally the power-armored marines at your back. You swear you can see her smile widen.

"女士！"她重複道。 "聽見了嗎？"她邊說邊回頭，身後的部下們正發出熱烈的歡呼聲。 "我們現在可是受人尊敬的公民了！"

A private channel opens on the fleet's command display. Isa is standing only a few steps away, but she has routed a live gallery feed from $shipTrophyIsaCompletionHomeName across the screen before saying anything.
The view settles on ranks of restored hulls beneath the gallery lights, each faction's doctrine preserved in steel, circuitry, and old scars.
"I wanted to see it from out here," Isa says at last. "The whole thing at once. One last time, before I leave."
"You've done it, Captain. The Hall of Triumph is done. Not finished, mind you; places like this are never finished. But every core ledger is preserved under one roof. Not under war, but peace."
Isa glances from the distant gallery to the fleet around you. "The Hall can preserve what came before. From here on, we get to make what comes next. Thank you for giving me a place in it."

Shattered Ring comes into view one broken section at a time.
Three vast arcs circle the barren moon below, each turning at a slightly different rate. Pressurized bridges, cargo gantries, and naked lengths of structural cable span some of the gaps. Others remain open to space, their severed ends capped with bulkheads scavenged from old ships.
The self-governing colony looks less constructed than prevented from falling apart. Isa appears beside the navigation station and plants both hands on your navigator’s desk.
"Take us around the dark side."
Your navigator glances at the approach plot.
"Traffic beacon’s directing us sunward."
"That traffic beacon’s been wrong since I was twelve."

這座自治殖民地，與其說是經過建造，不如說是勉強避免了分崩離析。 艾薩出現在導航站旁，雙手撐在你的導航員桌上。

By the time you reach the main concourse, word has spread.
Dockworkers call to Isa from the overhead gantries. A food vendor reaches across his counter to press a foil-wrapped pastry into her hand. Someone shouts that the recycler on Level Six is making the drinking water taste metallic again.
A child in an oversized pressure suit runs up and presents her with a cracked maneuvering thruster valve. Isa crouches, turns it over in her hands, and tells him which seal needs replacing.
Before you have crossed half the concourse, one of your bodyguards is carrying a crate of machine parts for an elderly mechanic. Another is holding a ladder steady while Isa points out a flickering light panel for an electrician.
Nobody has asked who you are.

當你抵達主大廳時，消息已經傳開了。
碼頭工人從頭頂的吊臂上向艾薩呼喊。一名食物攤販越過檯面，將一個錫箔紙包裹的糕點塞進她的手中。 有人大喊，六樓的回收機又讓飲用水帶有金屬味了。
一個身穿過大壓力服的孩子跑過來，遞給她一個裂開的機動推進器閥門。 艾薩蹲下身子，將閥門在手中翻來覆去地端詳，並告訴那孩子哪個密封圈需要更換。
在你還未走過中庭一半的距離時，其中一名保鑣正為一位年邁的機械師搬運一箱機器零件。 另一名保鑣正穩穩地扶著梯子，而艾薩則向一名電工指著一塊閃爍的燈光面板。

An old salvage foreman is waiting when Isa climbs down.
He wears a patched station utility suit, its original insignia hidden beneath decades of repairs. Under one arm, he carries a narrow metal case marked with faded cryogenic-handling symbols.
Isa’s good humor disappears.
"Where did you get that?"
"Found it behind the plating in Calder’s old storeroom," the foreman says. "Station council was clearing out abandoned property."
He holds the case toward her.
The people passing through the concourse give the three of you a wide berth. Finally, Isa wipes her hands against her trousers and accepts the case.
"Thanks."

entries.source:
Isa leads you through the station without speaking.
You descend through Arc Two, past hydroponics bays and crowded habitation decks, until the finished corridors give way to exposed conduits and old pressure doors.
The gravity weakens with each level.
Isa adjusts automatically, shortening her steps whenever the deck shifts beneath her. Your bodyguards are less graceful. One catches the overhead piping to avoid drifting into a wall.
At last, Isa opens an abandoned machine shop.
Several names have been carved into the pressure door. Hers is among them, scratched low enough that whoever wrote it must have been very young.
ISA LESESTER IS DA BEST.

"My great claim to fame," Isa says, smiling. "Youngest ‘pod person’ on my Arc."
A small metal contact is visible beneath the scorched collar.
Isa stops smiling.
"That wasn’t there before."
She releases the preservation seal and carefully lifts the suit onto the workbench. The fabric crackles as she turns the collar over, shedding small flecks of decayed plastic onto the surface below.
The frayed insulation has exposed an identification wafer embedded beneath the name strip.
Isa removes her slate.
On scan, her slate’s display splits into dozens of windows. Her delta-level AI agents begin testing ancient authentication protocols, interpolating damaged sectors, and comparing the wafer against surviving Domain registries.
"You don’t have to stay," she says.

她沉默了一陣子。那套舊制服仍攤開在你們之間的工作台上，艾薩克·萊斯特的名字在領口下方已褪色變黑，但仍可辨識。
她合上登記簿。
"船長。"
她的語氣已不復先前那份輕快。
"我知道這不關艦隊的事。"
她將一隻手搭在金屬箱上。
"但有人費了很大功夫才將他埋葬。 人之領INFOSEC、舊登記簿上的鎖，以及那些紀錄中殘存的任何內容。我覺得靠自己恐怕難以再深入調查了。"
艾薩直視著你。
"我想查明艾薩克·萊斯特究竟是誰。 他究竟發生了什麼事。為什麼要把我關進那個艙室。"
她猶豫了一下。
"我也想請你幫忙。"
entries.backTranslation:
Isa copied the surviving records onto her tablet.
She was silent for a moment. That old uniform was still spread out on the workbench between you; Isaac Lester’s name below the collar had faded to black but was still legible.
She closed the logbook.
" Captain. "
Her tone no longer had its earlier lightness.
" I know this isn’t the Fleet’s business. "
She rested one hand on the metal box.
" But someone went to great lengths to bury him. The Human Territory INFOSEC, the lock on the old registry, and whatever remains of those records. I don’t think I can investigate any further on my own. "
Isaac is staring straight at you.
" I want to find out who Isaac Lester really is. What exactly happened to him. Why he locked me in that cabin. "
She hesitated for a moment.
" I’d also like to ask for your help. "

The scan does not come from one direction. It blooms across every active sensor at once, measuring your fleet from two mutually impossible angles.
Cherubim and Lahat Haharev pivot in exact counterpoint. No hail follows. No warning asks you to keep your distance.
Your own identification packet returns instead, stripped of its header and divided into two mirrored copies.

entries.source:
The second hypershunt is already under attack.
Pather demolition ships cling to one of the collector spines. Shaped charges crawl across the black superstructure in glittering chains while scripture floods every open frequency: condemnation of the machine and promises of cleansing fire.
Across the structure, pirate cutting rigs have anchored directly to the transmission vanes. Industrial lasers bite into armor thick enough to roof cities. Salvage tugs wait behind them with their holds open, ready to carry off whatever the crews can tear loose before the Pathers bring the whole structure down.
The two flotillas fire past one another, each too committed to its work to disengage.
Isa sees the charge telemetry.
"No."
She enlarges the carrier spine, watching warning glyphs multiply across the projection.
"This is the only clue we have left. If they destroy that spine, Isaac's record goes with it."
The first Pather charge arms. A pirate tug wrenches a glowing section of armor away from the hypershunt.
The ship carrying Isa rolls out of formation before you can answer.
"Helm, bring us in. All batteries, engage. Get them away from my hypershunt."
entries.target:
第二條超空間通道已遭受襲擊。
帕瑟號爆破艦正緊貼著其中一根集能脊樑。 成串閃爍的成形炸藥沿著漆黑的上層結構蠕動，同時聖經經文淹沒了所有開放頻道：譴責機器，並承諾淨化之火。
在整個結構上，海盜切割裝置已直接錨定於傳輸葉片上。工業級雷射正咬噬著足以覆蓋整座城市的厚重裝甲。 打撈拖船在後方敞開貨艙待命，準備在帕瑟號摧毀整座結構之前，運走船員們能撕扯下來的任何殘骸。
兩支艦隊的火力交錯而過，雙方都過於專注於各自的任務而無法脫離交戰。
艾薩看到炸藥的遙測資料。
"不。"
她放大航母主樑的影像，看著警告符號在投影上不斷增生。
"這是我們僅存的線索。如果他們摧毀那條主幹，艾薩克的紀錄也將隨之消失。"
第一枚帕瑟炸彈已裝填完畢。一艘海盜拖船將超空間分流器上發光的裝甲段強行扯下。
在你來得及回應之前，載有艾薩的飛船已脫離編隊。
"舵手，將我們駛入。所有炮台，開火。把他們從我的超空間分流器旁趕走。"

" This is our only lead. If they destroy that main beam, Isaac’s records will vanish along with it. "

" Helmsman, steer us in. All turrets, fire. Drive them away from my hyperspace diverter. "

entries.source:
You lower your voice.
"The machine is not the object of our pilgrimage. We seek only what the servants of Moloch tried to bury within it."
You speak of false wonders, poisoned knowledge, and the duty of the faithful to expose the sins of the old Domain without claiming its power for themselves.
The commander studies you for a long moment.
At last, he nods.
"Then go, brother. For the Prophet’s sake, go."
The Pather fleet begins clearing the approach corridor.
entries.target:
你壓低了聲音。
"這台機器並非我們朝聖的目標。 我們只尋求摩洛克的僕從試圖將其深埋其中的東西。"
你談論的是虛假的奇蹟、被毒化的知識，以及信徒的職責——揭露舊人之領的罪孽，卻不為自己奪取其力量。
指揮官凝視著你許久。
最後，他點了點頭。
"那麼去吧，兄弟。 為了先知的緣故，去吧。"

"Then go, brother. For the sake of the Prophet, go. "

After your fleet docks.
Then you explain what happens to pirates who demand payment before the customer is surrounded, stationary, and attached to something fragile.

entries.source:
With the approach corridor clear, your fleet closes on the hypershunt.
The structure grows across the forward display until it no longer resembles a machine. Black towers rise through the stellar corona, joined by collector vanes and transmission spines large enough to eclipse cities. Streams of plasma bend around it in slow, incandescent arches.
Isa stands beside the sensor station, slate in hand.
"We’ll need to map the whole thing."
She begins assigning survey patterns across the fleet.
"Field geometry. Collector alignment. Residual phase harmonics. Anything the Domain tuned by hand."
entries.target:
隨著進場航道已清空，你的艦隊正逼近超空間轉接點。
該結構在前方顯示螢幕上逐漸放大，直至不再像一台機器。黑色高塔從恆星日冕中拔地而起，其間交織著集熱葉片與傳輸脊柱，其規模之大足以遮蔽整座城市。 等離子流以緩慢而熾熱的弧線環繞其周身。
艾薩站在感測站旁，手中握著石板。
"我們需要繪製這座結構的完整地圖。"
她開始向艦隊各處分配勘測模式。
"場域幾何結構。收集器的對齊狀態。 殘餘相位諧波。任何由人之領親手調校過的項目。"
entries.backTranslation:
With the approach corridor now clear, your fleet is closing in on the hyperspace waypoint.
The structure gradually grows larger on the forward display until it no longer resembles a machine. A black tower rises from the stellar corona, interwoven with heat-collecting blades and transmission spines, its scale vast enough to obscure an entire city. Streams of plasma encircle it in slow, searing arcs.
Isa stands beside the sensor station, a tablet in her hand.
" We need to map this structure in its entirety. "
She began assigning survey modes to various sections of the fleet.
" Field geometry. Collector alignment. Residual phase harmonics. Any items personally calibrated by the Ren people. "

entries.source:
Your fleet spends several days circling the hypershunt.
Sensor craft trace the curvature of its containment fields. Gravimetric probes measure distortions along the transmission spines. Isa’s agents compare the results against surviving Domain engineering standards and the concealed routing data recovered at Shattered Ring.
Most of the structure follows standard automated tolerances.
Several sections do not.

該結構的大部分符合標準的自動化公差範圍。
但有幾個區段則不符合。

Most of the structure falls within standard automated tolerance ranges.
However, several sections do not comply.

entries.source:
Tiny deviations recur across the hypershunt’s oldest assemblies: corrections too consistent to be random, repeated through construction phases separated by centuries.
Isa overlays them.
A familiar authorization pattern emerges from the accumulated calibration data.
DCR-2F38-CB017-6A
LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
CONTINUITY AUTHORITY
Isa leans closer.
"That’s him."
The same pattern appears in the hypershunt’s transmission geometry, attached to a routing vector concealed beneath SUPER ALABASTER restriction.
[A sealed personal log is embedded beside the routing data.]

艾薩將這些資料疊加分析。
從累積的校準資料中浮現出一種熟悉的授權模式。

萊斯特， 艾薩克·托馬斯
延續管理局

相同的模式出現在超空間分流器的傳輸幾何結構中，附著於隱藏在SUPER ALABASTER限制下的路由向量上。

entries.source:
The recording terminates abruptly.
Isa does not move.
The hypershunt burns across the forward display behind her, its black superstructure suspended within the stellar corona.
After a long silence, she looks down at the microchip connected to her slate.
"His daughter."
She swallows.
"They were supposed to wake her together."
Her eyes move back over the revival report.
"Rebecca died, and he never opened the other pod."
entries.target:
錄音突然中斷。
艾薩一動也不動。
超空間分流在她的前方顯示幕上灼燒而過，其黑色上層結構懸浮於恆星日冕之中。
經過漫長的沉默，她低頭望向連接在她平板上的微晶片。
"他的女兒。"
她吞了口口水。
"他們本該一起將她喚醒。"
她的目光又移回復甦報告上。
"蕾貝卡死了，而他從未打開另一具艙體。"
entries.backTranslation:
The recording suddenly cut off.
Isa stood motionless.
The hyperspace bypass blazed across the display screen in front of her, its black superstructure suspended within the stellar corona.
After a long silence, she looked down at the microchip connected to her tablet.
" His daughter. "
She swallowed hard.
" They were supposed to wake her up together. "
Her gaze shifted back to the resuscitation report.
" Rebecca was dead, and he had never opened the other pod. "

entries.source:
The carrier signal continues repeating beneath the silence.
Isa scrolls back through the recovered fragments, reading the same lines again.
"He never named her."
"I know," she says before you can answer.
Isa grips the edge of her slate.
"The suit. His identification. This log, somehow encoded within the Hypershunt. All of it was meant to be a message to... to me."
She shakes her head.
"But my pod was opened centuries after this was recorded. I don’t know what happened between."
She stares at the carrier trace.
"Or was he trying to come back?"
entries.target:
載波訊號在寂靜中持續迴盪。
艾薩向後捲動已恢復的片段，再次閱讀相同的內容。
"他從未給她取過名字。"
"我知道，" 她在你來得及回答前說道。
艾薩緊握著石板的邊緣。
"那套制服。他的身分證明。這份日誌，不知為何被編碼在超空間轉接器之中。這一切原本都是要傳達給……傳達給我的訊息。"
她搖了搖頭。
"但我的艙體是在這段記錄完成數世紀後才被開啟的。我不知道這期間發生了什麼。"
她凝視著載波軌跡。
"還是他試圖回來？"
entries.backTranslation:
The carrier signal continued to echo in the silence.
Isa scrolled back through the recovered fragments and reread the same content.
" He had never given her a name. "
" I know, " she said before you could answer.
Isa gripped the edge of the stone tablet tightly.
" That uniform. His ID. This log—for some reason, it was encoded within the hyperspace relay. All of this was originally meant to be conveyed to… conveyed to me. "
She shook her head.
" But my pod wasn't opened until centuries after this recording was completed. I don't know what happened during that time. "
She stared at the carrier’s trajectory.
" Or was he trying to come back? "

"The message is riding the same transmission geometry as the classified routing signal."
She separates the two patterns. A narrow vector appears on the tactical display, extending away from the hypershunt and into unexplored space.
"This gives us direction."
Isa enlarges the projection and looks toward the location of the remaining hypershunt.
"We need the other signal."

[Filed under Gan Eden Archives in Intel.]
[The first hypershunt routing vector has been recovered.]

"這則訊息正沿著與機密路由訊號相同的傳輸幾何路徑傳輸。"
她將這兩種模式分開。 戰術螢幕上出現一道狹窄的向量，從超空間分流點延伸而出，深入未探索的太空。
"這為我們指明了方向。"
艾薩放大投影畫面，朝著剩餘超空間分流器的方位望去。
"我們需要另一個訊號。"
[已恢復的日誌 — 第二部分。]

entries.backTranslation:
Aisa returned to the carrier’s data.
" This message is being transmitted along the same transmission geometry path as the classified routing signal. "
She separated the two patterns. A narrow vector appeared on the tactical screen, extending from the hyperspace junction point and deep into unexplored space.
" This points us in the right direction. "
Aisa zoomed in on the projection and looked toward the location of the remaining hyperspace diverter.
" We need another signal. "
[Recovered Log — Part Two.]
[Archived under the Intelligence category in the Eden Archives.]
[First hyperspace diversion path vector recovered.]

Cloud systems drift across continents suspended impossibly above you, their shadows moving over forests and inland seas.
There is no horizon in any direction. Only a solar-system sized, singular world.
There are no words to say. You see several of your bridge members reach out to hug each other.
Then every alarm on Isa's slate goes off at once.

entries.source:
Your fleet touches down beneath the Tree of Life.
For a while, nobody seems to know what to do.
The landing grounds lie beneath a vast canopy of living green, the trunks rising between grey, uniform towers and terraces until the branches close together overhead like the roof of a cathedral. Warm air moves through the open ramps carrying the smell of soil, leaves, and water.
Requests for shore leave begin almost immediately.
By the time the first reports reach you, entire deck crews are offering detailed explanations for why their particular ship can absolutely spare them for an hour.
Your captains recommend a compromise: short rotating leave. The schedule is approved with suspicious enthusiasm.
When the first rotation comes down the ramps, some of the spacers simply stop.
entries.target:
你的艦隊降落在生命之樹下方。
過了一會兒，似乎沒人知道該怎麼辦。
著陸場位於一片遼闊的翠綠樹冠之下，樹幹從灰色的、整齊劃一的塔樓與露台之間聳立而起，枝椏在頭頂交織簇擁，宛如大教堂的穹頂。 暖風穿過敞開的舷梯，帶來泥土、樹葉與水的氣息。
上岸休假的申請幾乎立刻就開始了。
當第一份報告傳到你手中時，整個甲板船員都已準備好詳細解釋，說明為何他們的船絕對能抽調他們一小時。
你的船長們建議一個折衷方案：短期的輪流休假。 這項排程以令人起疑的熱忱獲得批准。
當第一批輪班人員沿著斜坡走下時，部分太空人竟直接停下了腳步。
entries.backTranslation:
Your fleet has landed beneath the Tree of Life.
After a moment, it seemed no one knew what to do.
The landing pad lies beneath a vast, emerald canopy of trees, their trunks rising between gray, uniform towers and terraces, their branches intertwining overhead like the dome of a cathedral. A warm breeze swept through the open gangway, carrying the scent of earth, leaves, and water.
Requests for shore leave began almost immediately.
By the time the first report reached you, the entire deck crew was ready to explain in detail why their ship could absolutely spare them for an hour.
Your captains proposed a compromise: short, rotating leave periods. This schedule was approved with suspicious enthusiasm.
As the first group of shift workers walked down the ramp, some of the astronauts actually stopped in their tracks.

entries.source:
Most have seen nothing but hydroponics decks and cramped crew quarters their entire lives. Some have even visited abundant worlds like Gilead. The ones who have not walk out into the grass and lie down in it, staring up through the branches into the strange, inverted shell-sky.
Before long, the landing grounds are dotted with off-duty crew doing exactly the same thing. Some of them start a kickball match.
You make a mental note to have the watches keep careful count when each rotation returns. AWOL incidents would be epidemic. Isa stands at the foot of the ramp, staring upward.
For once, she seems to have forgotten the slate in her hand.
entries.target:
大多數人一生所見的，僅有水耕栽培甲板和擁擠的船員艙室。有些人甚至曾造訪過像 Gilead 這般物產豐饒的世界。那些未曾造訪過的人，會走進草地躺下，透過樹枝間的縫隙仰望那奇異、倒置的貝殼般天空。
沒過多久，著陸場上便零星出現了正在做同樣事情的休班船員。其中一些人開始進行一場踢球比賽。
你暗自提醒自己，每當輪班返回時，要讓值班人員仔細清點人數。 擅離崗位的情況恐怕會如瘟疫般蔓延。艾薩站在斜坡底部，抬頭凝視著上方。
難得地，她似乎忘記了手上的石板。
entries.backTranslation:
For most people, the extent of their life’s experience is limited to hydroponic decks and cramped crew quarters. Some have even visited bountiful worlds like Gilead. Those who have never visited such places would walk out onto the grass, lie down, and gaze up through the gaps in the branches at that strange, upside-down, shell-like sky.
Before long, off-duty crew members began to appear sporadically on the landing pad, doing the same thing. Some of them began playing a game of soccer.
You silently reminded yourself to have the crew on duty conduct a thorough headcount whenever a shift returned. Absences from duty would likely spread like a plague. Aisa stood at the bottom of the slope, looking up at the sky above.
For once, she seemed to have forgotten the slate in her hand.

The settlement known as the Tree of Life is cleaner than anything has a right to be.
There are no sweepers, no maintenance crews, no little machines trundling along the paths like you might see at Tritachyon. Dust simply does not seem to settle. Water leaves no trace on the pale walls or glass, and fallen leaves collect in neat lines along the edges of the walkways, as though the city itself knows where they belong.
At the larger intersections, broad basins of crystal-clear water descend into deep reservoirs placed in the middle of the streets. Your suit's scanners immediately flag it as drinkable—almost absurdly free of contaminants.

Inside, Gan Eden’s perfection finally gives way to something unmistakably human. Tools cover the benches. Components have been dismantled and rebuilt by hand. A narrow cot has been pushed against one wall, and beside it sits a small table with a teapot still resting on top.
Isa lifts the lid.
The inside is bone dry, with a dark ring of residue clinging to the bottom.
She puts it down carefully.
"He lived here."
One wall has been covered in calculations. At first they look like ordinary power-transfer notes. Isa studies them for several seconds, then steps closer. Hypershunt output frequencies have been broken apart and recombined alongside communications theory, with tiny variations marked through the carrier harmonics.

The Space Elevator rises from the inner surface into the atmosphere above Gan Eden. Its upper terminus remains dark, but the structure itself is intact.
Your fleet begins a cautious approach.
Two strange Omega Shards emerge from the atmospheric glare. They cross the approach corridor without hailing, their overlapping drive fields building a wall of impossible vectors ahead of you.
Every attempt to advance turns into lateral acceleration. Dampers scream. Navigation gives ground before the fleet is thrown bodily into the elevator's outer superstructure.
The Shards hold until you retreat, then disappear back into the curve of the world.

entries.source:
With Cherubim and Lahat Ha-Cherev gone, the elevator's interdiction field is silent.
Isa's inherited suit transponder opens the outer doors.
The landing dock beyond is empty except for the wreck of a Kite shuttle, driven hard against one side of the platform. Its entire right wing was scorched away and much of the hull has been melted into slag by some enormous burst of energy. You have a fairly good idea which of the two constructs was responsible.
A dark trail begins beside the shattered cockpit. Nearly two centuries have reduced it to little more than a stain against the deck, but it continues away from the wreck and into the elevator, uneven and unmistakable.
Something dragged itself from the shuttle.
Your bodyguards and Isa follow the trail through the silent corridors toward the master control room. It ends in the hallway outside.
That is where Isaac Thomas Leicester is.
His remains lie against the wall, still sealed inside a vacuum suit. The helmet is cracked across the visor, and there is nothing visible within except darkness. An identification transponder on his back continues to pulse after all these years.
LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS.
Beside him lies a recording unit.
Isa sucks in a breath and drops to her knees beside the suit. Tears are already running down her face by the time she reaches toward him, stopping just short of touching the cracked helmet.
"The last log."
LOG — FINAL

對面的停靠碼頭空無一物，唯有一架風箏號穿梭機的殘骸，猛烈地撞在平台的側壁上。其整個右側機翼已被燒蝕殆盡，機身大部分也因某種巨大的能量爆發而熔化成熔渣。 你大致能猜到是哪個構造體所為。
一道暗色痕跡從破碎的駕駛艙旁延伸而出。近兩個世紀的歲月已使其幾乎只剩甲板上的汙漬，但這道痕跡仍從殘骸處延伸至電梯內，雖不規則卻清晰可辨。
有東西從太空梭裡拖著自己爬了出來。
你的保鑣和艾薩循著這道痕跡，穿過寂靜的走廊，朝主控制室前進。 這條痕跡終點就在外面的走廊上。
艾薩克·托馬斯·萊斯特就在那裡。
他的遺體倚靠著牆壁，仍被密封在真空服內。 頭盔的護目鏡橫向裂開，內部除了黑暗之外什麼也看不見。他背上的識別應答器，經過這麼多年依然持續脈動。
萊斯特，艾薩克·托馬斯。
他身旁放著一台錄影裝置。
艾薩深吸一口氣，跪倒在太空服旁。 當她伸手向他靠近時，淚水早已順著臉頰滑落，手在即將觸碰到那頂裂開的頭盔前停了下來。
"最後的日誌。"
LOG — 完
entries.backTranslation:
With the disappearance of Cherubim and Rahat Ha-Cherief, the elevator’s force field has fallen silent. The transponder in the spacesuit
Isa inherited activated the outer door.
The docking bay opposite her was empty, save for the wreckage of a Kite-class shuttle that had crashed violently into the sidewall of the platform. Its entire right wing had been completely burned away, and most of the fuselage had been melted into slag by some massive energy burst. You can probably guess which construct was responsible.
A dark trail extended from beside the shattered cockpit. Nearly two centuries have reduced it to little more than a stain on the deck, but the trail still extends from the wreckage into the elevator—irregular yet clearly discernible.
Something dragged itself out of the shuttle.
Your bodyguard and Isaac followed the trail through the silent corridor toward the main control room. The trail ended right there in the outer corridor.
Isaac Thomas Lester is right there.
His body was leaning against the wall, still sealed inside his spacesuit. The visor of his helmet was cracked horizontally; nothing but darkness could be seen inside. The identification transponder on his back continued to pulse, even after all these years.
Lester, Isaac Thomas.
A video recorder lay beside him.
Isaac took a deep breath and knelt beside the spacesuit. As she reached out toward him, tears were already streaming down her cheeks, and her hand paused just before it touched the cracked helmet.
" Final Log. "
LOG — End

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART I
My name is Isaac Thomas Leicester, Director of Engineering for Heliostructural Systems in the Persean Sector.
My work included the construction of the coronal hypershunts and, later, Project Eden.
The projects were expected to take centuries. Eden might have required more than a thousand years before reaching its final design capacity. No ordinary succession of administrators could preserve the technical knowledge, institutional memory, and design intent required over such a span.
The Domain therefore established a continuity office. Its directors would serve across generations, entering cryosuspension between major phases of construction and returning whenever the work required their judgment.
I was elected to lead it.
The appointment required me to spend hundreds of years at a time in cryosuspension. I would sleep through epochs of construction, wake for major design reviews, inspect the work and approve the next phase.
The first hypershunt was already under construction when I accepted the appointment. It was intended to collect energy directly from a star and make that power available to automated construction systems far beyond any ordinary network.
The engineering difficulties were substantial.
The structure had to remain stable inside a star’s corona. Its collection systems had to survive constant radiation and violent changes in stellar activity. The transfer network had to carry more power in one moment than entire inhabited systems had ever consumed.
We lost dozens of unmanned assembly swarms before completing the first stable framework.
The second hypershunt was approved before the first reached full capacity. Its design incorporated everything we had learned. Construction proceeded more quickly, although centuries still passed outside my chamber.
Each waking period lasted several months, even years. I met engineers whose grandparents had worked under engineers I remembered. I approved changes to systems designed by people who had passed while I slept. The Domain expanded between each waking.
New systems joined the Gate network. Problems once considered impossible became trivial. I believed I was watching humanity mature, but I did not yet understand what was being lost.
When two hypershunts became operational, the Directorate approved the project they had been built to support.
I proposed the name Gan Eden, after the sacred garden of God.
It was to be the Domain’s first enclosed—
DOMAIN INFOSEC VIOLATION THRESHOLD WARNING
// datastream resetting...
—constructed around a yellow sun on the far outskirts of the Persean Sector. At its intended capacity, it could shelter several quintillion human li—
FATAL ACCESS ERROR //
This device is not authorized to provide additional description of the referenced project, destination, or design objective. Please upgrade your data permission level in compliance with Domain Information Security Standards.
I believed that the ability to construct such a wonder proved that the Domain deserved to continue expanding.
I was wrong.

已復原個人日誌
作者：萊斯特，艾薩克·托馬斯
檔案：日誌 — 第一部分
我的名字是艾薩克·托馬斯·萊斯特，現任珀爾修斯星區日構系統公司工程總監。
我的工作包括建造日冕超迴路，以及後來的伊甸園計畫。
這些計畫預計將耗時數世紀。伊甸園可能需要超過一千年的時間才能達到其最終設計容量。 在如此漫長的時空中，普通的行政人員更替根本無法保存所需的技術知識、組織記憶以及設計意圖。
因此，人之領設立了延續辦公室。 其主任將跨越數代任職，在主要施工階段之間進入冷凍休眠狀態，並於工程需要其判斷時隨時歸來。
我獲選領導該辦公室。
這項任命要求我每次需在冷凍休眠狀態中度過數百年。 我將在各建設時期中處於冷凍休眠狀態，僅在重大設計審查時甦醒，檢查工程進度並批准下一階段。
當我接受這項任命時，第一條超空間分流管已開始動工。 其設計目的是直接從恆星收集能量，並將這股動力輸送給遠超乎任何普通網絡範圍的自動化建造系統。
工程上的難度極大。
該結構必須在恆星日冕內保持穩定。 其能量收集系統必須能承受持續的輻射以及恆星活動的劇烈變化。 傳輸網路必須在瞬間承載的電力，甚至超過所有有人居住的星系至今為止的總消耗量。
在完成第一個穩定框架之前，我們損失了數十個無人組裝群。
第二座超空間分流器在第一座尚未達到滿載容量之前便已獲准動工。 其設計融合了我們迄今所學的一切。儘管在我的密室之外仍已過去數世紀，建造進度卻更加迅速。
每次清醒期都持續數個月，甚至數年之久。我遇見了那些祖父母曾在我記憶中的工程師麾下工作的工程師。 我批准了那些在我沉睡期間已然離世之人所設計的系統變更。在每次清醒期間之間，人之領不斷擴張。
新的系統加入了星門網絡。 過去被視為無法解決的問題，如今已微不足道。我以為自己正在見證人類的成熟，卻尚未明白究竟失去了什麼。
當兩條超空間捷徑投入運作後，總局批准了為支援這些捷徑而建的專案。
我提議將其命名為伊甸園，以紀念上帝的神聖花園。
這將是人之領首座封閉式——
人之領 INFOSEC 違規閾值警告
// 資料流重置中……
——這座設施環繞著一顆黃色太陽建造，位於佩爾塞亞星區的最外緣。 若達到預定容量，它可容納數千兆萬億人類——
致命存取錯誤 //
本裝置未獲授權提供有關所引用專案、目的地或設計目標的進一步說明。 請依照人之領資訊安全標準，升級您的資料權限等級。
我曾相信，能夠建造如此奇蹟的能力，證明了人之領值得繼續擴張。
我錯了。

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART II
Before the continuity office was established, I lived at Telepylus Station with my wife, Rebecca Anne Sarai.
Rebecca was a senior engineer in stellar-transfer architecture. The Directorate offered us joint appointments: I as Director of the continuity office, Rebecca as its Chief Integration Engineer.
We intended to serve the entire tenure together, entering cryosuspension between construction phases and waking side by side whenever the work required us.
Our daughter was born shortly before the first long suspension interval. We placed her pediatric chamber beside our own, intending to wake and raise her during every active interval.
At the first scheduled revival, I woke.
Rebecca did not survive the thaw.
Complications from cryosuspension caused a permanent psychosomatic rupture. I had her euthanized the day I got the prognosis.
From then on, I accepted sole leadership, promising that I would finish the work and wake my daughter into the world Rebecca and I had intended for her.
I vowed to forever keep my daughter safe. Not until I, with my own hands, could ensure the world could not take her away from me like God did Rebecca.
I hate myself.
I hate myself.
I hate myself—

已復原的個人日誌
作者：萊斯特，艾薩克·托馬斯
檔案： 日誌 — 第二部分
在延續辦公室成立之前，我與妻子蕾貝卡·安妮·莎拉伊居住於 Telepylus 空間站。
蕾貝卡是恆星轉移建築領域的高級工程師。 總局向我們提供了聯合任命：我擔任延續辦公室主任，蕾貝卡則擔任該辦公室的首席整合工程師。
我們原打算共同完成整個任期，在各建設階段之間進入冷凍休眠，並在工作需要時並肩甦醒。
我們的女兒在第一次長期冷凍休眠期開始前不久出生。 我們把她的兒童冷凍艙放在我們艙室旁邊，打算在每個工作期間都醒來並撫養她。
在第一次預定的復甦時，我醒了。
蕾貝卡在解凍過程中未能存活。
冷凍懸浮引起的併發症導致她出現永久性的心身功能斷裂。 在收到預後診斷的那天，我便安排讓她接受安樂死。
從那時起，我接手了獨自領導的職責，並承諾將完成這項工作，讓我的女兒甦醒，進入蕾貝卡和我為她所規劃的世界。
我發誓要永遠守護女兒的安全。 直到我能親手確保這個世界無法像上帝帶走蕾貝卡那樣，將她從我身邊奪走為止。
我恨自己。
我恨自己。
我恨自己——

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART III
My daughter remained unchanged. I made certain of it.
At every waking, the physicians offered to revive her. At every waking, I refused. I visited her chamber, reviewed the medical reports, and repeated tests the technicians had already completed while centuries passed outside.
The Domain did not remain unchanged.
I saw a decay. The soul of Man gangrenous and rotting.
I met an Armada veteran cleaning coolant residue from a station floor. A reactor leak had destroyed half his face. His pension had been suspended because the archive containing his service record no longer existed.
I offered to help. He asked only that I help his daughter obtain a transit permit.
Seventy-two years passed. I never found out what happened to him or his daughter.
Nothing changed.
During another waking period, I met a woman who had spent years moving between ports because she could not obtain employment without proof of residence, or residence without proof of employment. The station classified her as a transient clearance burden.
Years blurred together. I can't tell if it was the repeated cryosuspensions or my deteriorating mind, but at some point I couldn't distinguish faces. I even forgot Rebecca's face.
I remembered the facts of her: the scar at her wrist, the hymn she hummed while she worked, the way she squeezed my hand when she was frightened. But whenever I tried to assemble those memories into a face, there was only an absence where my wife had been.
Rebecca.
You understood this before I did. You once told me that the Domain was the greatest work of man that had ever been made, and that was why it was so grotesque.
I began speaking publicly. At first, I presented reports and projections. The Directorate thanked me and established a commission.
Nothing changed.
I said that human beings were not obsolete machinery. I said that a civilization should be judged by those it could help and chose not to. I said that every person carried the image of God, whether or not the Domain could locate the correct record for them.
People began gathering to hear me. The gatherings became demonstrations. Security forces were deployed. People were injured, then killed.
I continued speaking, but I don't know why. With my mouth I drove lambs to the slaughter, and with my hands and my work I forged the knives the Domain of Man plunged into their necks.
Who was I?
No one. I was a worthless hypocrite.
I spoke out against the great Whore of Babylon whilst I remained her greatest slave.
Nothing changed.
entries.target:
已恢復的個人日誌
作者：萊斯特，艾薩克·托馬斯
檔案：日誌 — 第三部分
我的女兒依然如故。 我已確認這一點。
每次她甦醒時，醫師們都提議要讓她復甦。每次她甦醒時，我都拒絕了。我前往她的病房，檢視醫療報告，並重複技術人員早已完成的檢測，而外界的時光卻已流逝數世紀。
人之領卻並非一成不變。
我目睹了腐朽。人類的靈魂已然潰爛腐敗。
我遇見了一位曾參與阿馬達行動的老兵，他正在清理空間站地板上的冷卻劑殘留物。 反應爐洩漏摧毀了他半張臉。由於記載他服役紀錄的檔案庫已不復存在，他的退休金被暫停發放。
我主動提出協助。他只要求我幫他的女兒取得過境許可證。
七十二年過去了。 我始終無從得知他和女兒的下落。
一切依舊。
在另一次清醒期間，我遇見了一位女子，她多年來輾轉於各個港口之間，因為她既無法在沒有居住證明的情況下獲得工作，也無法在沒有工作證明的情況下取得居住許可。 空間站將她歸類為過境通關負擔。
歲月模糊地交疊在一起。我無法確定是反覆的冷凍休眠，還是我日漸衰退的思維所致，但到了某個時刻，我已無法辨認面孔。 我甚至連蕾貝卡的臉都忘了。
我還記得關於她的點點滴滴：她手腕上的疤痕、她工作時哼唱的聖詩、她害怕時緊握我手的方式。 但每當我試圖將這些記憶拼湊成一張臉時，我妻子曾經所在之處，卻只剩下一片空虛。
蕾貝卡。
你比我更早明白這一點。 你曾告訴我，人之領是人類有史以來最偉大的傑作，而這正是它如此怪誕的原因。
我開始公開發言。 起初，我僅提出報告與預測。總署向我致謝，並成立了一個委員會。
但一切都沒有改變。
我說，人類並非過時的機器。 我則表示，一個文明應以其本可幫助卻選擇不幫助的對象來衡量。我說，無論人之領能否為他們找出正確的紀錄，每個人都承載著神的形象。
人們開始聚集聆聽我的話語。這些聚會逐漸演變成示威遊行。安全部隊隨即被部署。 有人受傷，隨後有人喪生。
我繼續講話，但我不知道為什麼。 我用嘴將羔羊驅向屠宰場，又用雙手與我的勞動，鍛造出人之領刺入他們頸項的利刃。
我究竟是誰？
無足輕重之人。 我不過是個一文不值的偽君子。
我 公開譴責那偉大的巴比倫大淫婦，而我卻仍是她最忠實的奴隸。
一切都沒有改變。

Author: Lester, Isaac Thomas

My daughter remains the same. I have confirmed this.
Every time she regains consciousness, the doctors suggest resuscitating her. Every time she regains consciousness, I refuse. I went to her ward, reviewed the medical reports, and repeated the tests the technicians had long since completed, while centuries had passed in the outside world.
Yet the human mind is not static.
I witnessed decay. The human soul has already rotted and decayed.

Everything remains the same.

You understood this before I did. You once told me that the Human Collar is humanity’s greatest masterpiece of all time, and that is precisely why it is so bizarre.
I began speaking publicly. At first, I merely presented reports and predictions. The General Administration thanked me and established a committee.

I continued to speak, though I did not know why. With my mouth, I drove the lambs to the slaughterhouse; with my hands and my labor, I forged the sharp blades that the Human Collar plunged into their necks.
Who am I, really?
A nobody. I am nothing but a worthless hypocrite.
I I publicly denounce the great Whore of Babylon, yet I remain her most faithful slave.
Nothing has changed.

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — PART IV
The Domain arrested me for insurrection.
At trial, they presented my speeches, correspondence, and engineering reports. I denied very little. When the Sector Governor asked whether I recognized the absolute authority of the Domain of Man, I told him that all human authority was subordinate to God.
They found me guilty.
I was kept under house arrest at Telepylus Station while preparations were made to return me to Sol for sentencing. They still needed my knowledge of Gan Eden, and some of its oldest systems continued to recognize my credentials.
Finally, I decided to end it.
For the first time in centuries, I authorized my daughter’s revival. She was so small. I could nearly palm her in my hand. With hands shaking, I fashioned a small cradle from my old spacer suit. My only inheritence to my prodigal daughter. Then I re-suspended her. It felt like burying Rebecca all over again.
Then I set my plot in motion.
The hypershunts supplied Gan Eden through the Gate network. Their full output passed through the rings as energy before reaching the sphere’s master control system. I would sieze a craft, pass through the Penelope’s Star Gate, enter the control complex, and redirect the full output of both hypershunts into Gan Eden.
The Gan Eden would be destroyed, and I with it.
I escaped confinement, commandeered the transport, and changed its destination after the transit sequence began.
Telepylus security had already identified the ship, and I expected the escort to follow me through the Gate within seconds. Instead, the patrol craft broke formation before they reached the ring. Traffic control began issuing emergency orders over one another, several ships stopped answering, and the Gate-status displays failed in rapid succession.
I did not know what had drawn their attention away from me, only that the route to Gan Eden was still open. I entered the coordinates, drove the transport through at maximum thrust, and emerged into the restricted system without pursuit. Gan Eden’s control network accepted my credentials immediately. I seized the approach corridor and pushed the ship toward the master control complex before whatever was happening at Penelope’s Star could close the way behind me.
Oh, Hosanna. Hosaana in the higehest.
Despite its hubris and its separation from God, Gan Eden was the most beautiful place in the entire universe.
Once inside the system, I abandoned the transport and took a shuttle to the master control complex at the space elevator. For less than a second, the system behaved exactly as I had intended.
Then the Gate network began shutting down around me.
The conduits carrying the hypershunt output vanished before the power could reach Gan Eden. With nowhere else to go, the discharge collapsed back through the nearest ring still connected to the transfer system: Penelope’s Star.
I watched the impossibility of Adamantine shattering like clay over telemetry and break apart. A moment later, every other Gate disappeared from the network.
I intended to die in Gan Eden.
Instead, I was left alive inside it.

已恢復的個人日誌
作者：萊斯特，艾薩克·托馬斯
檔案： 日誌 — 第四部分
人之領以叛亂罪名逮捕了我。
在審判中，他們出示了我的演講稿、書信往來及工程報告。 我幾乎沒有否認什麼。當分區總督問我是否承認人之領的絕對權威時，我告訴他，一切人類的權威都服從於上帝。
他們判定我有罪。
在準備將我送回索爾接受判決期間，我被軟禁在Telepylus 空間站。 他們仍需要我對伊甸園的知識，而且那裡部分最古老的系統仍能識別我的資格證明。
最後，我決定結束這一切。
數世紀以來首次，我授權讓女兒復活。她如此嬌小。 我幾乎可以將她整個人捧在掌心。我雙手顫抖著，用那套舊太空服為她製作了一個小小的搖籃。這是我留給這個浪子女兒的唯一遺產。接著，我將她重新置入冷凍艙。那種感覺，彷彿又是在重新埋葬蕾貝卡一般。
我開始執行計畫。
超空間分流器透過星門網路向伊甸園供能，其全部輸出先以能量形式通過光環，再送抵球體主控系統。 我將劫持一艘飛船，穿越 Penelope's Star 的星門，進入控制中心，並將兩條超空間分流器的全部輸出重新導向伊甸園。
伊甸園將會被摧毀，而我也將隨之毀滅。
我逃離了禁錮，強行接管了運輸船，並在傳送序列啟動後更改了目的地。
Telepylus 安全部門早已識別出這艘船，我預期護衛艦隊將在數秒內追隨我穿過星門。 然而，巡邏艦在抵達星門環之前便打破了隊形。 交通管制中心開始互相發送緊急指令，數艘飛船停止回應，而星門狀態顯示器也接連失靈。
我並不知道是什麼讓他們的注意力從我身上移開，只知道通往伊甸園的航線仍然暢通。 我輸入座標，以最大推力駕駛運輸船穿越星門，未遭追擊便進入了這片限制星系。伊甸園的控制網路立即接受了我的認證。我迅速佔據進場航道，並在 Penelope's Star 發生的任何事態來得及封鎖我身後的路之前，將飛船駛向主控制中心。
哦，和撒那。至高無上的和撒那。
儘管伊甸園充滿傲慢且與上帝疏離，它仍是整個宇宙中最美麗的地方。
進入該星系後，我棄置了運輸船，改乘穿梭機前往位於太空電梯旁的主控中心。 不到一秒鐘，系統運作完全符合我的預期。
接著，我周圍的星門網絡開始關閉。
傳輸超空間分流輸出信號的導管，在能量抵達伊甸園之前便已消失無蹤。 無處可去之下，放電流通過最近且仍與轉運系統相連的環狀結構——Penelope's Star——倒灌而回。
我透過遙測畫面目睹了本應堅不可摧之物如黏土般碎裂崩解。 片刻之後，其餘所有的星門都從網絡中消失了。
我本打算在伊甸園中死去。
然而，我卻活著被困在其中。

RECOVERED PERSONAL LOG
AUTHOR: LEICESTER, ISAAC THOMAS
FILE: LOG — FINAL
I am dying.
I have lived alone in Gan Eden for thirty-six years.
I spent the first several years searching the cities, shelters, maintenance tunnels, and transit stations. I transmitted on every emergency frequency that still worked.
No one answered. I knew no one would. The last human technicians had left Gan Eden centuries before, when its construction passed entirely to the automated swarms. I was the one who signed off on that order.
I eventually settled in this place I named Galilee, repaired one of the old agricultural houses, and learned to farm. When I was not working, I wandered the shell. I walked through empty cities, forests planted by machines, and coastlines no human being had ever seen. It is a never-ending day here, as if it were before God separated Light from Darkness.
Gan Eden remained beautiful.
Oh, God.
I also continued trying to restore the Gate connection to Penelope’s Star. At first, I told myself I was trying to rescue my daughter. I admit now that I only want to know whether I killed her.
Oh, my daughter.
Rebecca wanted to name you Leah.
To Leah, my beautiful daughter I never knew:
I said I saved you for a future I believed I could build. That was only partly true.
Every physician told me you could be revived. Every report said your chamber was sound. But whenever I imagined authorizing the thaw, I saw Rebecca dying on the revival table. I kept you asleep because I was afraid.
I dressed that fear in duty and chased my arrogant dream across centuries. Then, when the world failed to become what I envisioned, I abandoned you to your fate.
Neither you nor God owe me any forgiveness.
I prayed for you every day. I prayed for Rebecca. I prayed for the dead, and for the living I had condemned without ever knowing their names.
I do not know whether God heard me.
Until today.
Today, God finally answered.
It did not connect to Penelope’s Star or any other Gate I knew. Instead, two angels arrived through the the Earth and began ascending toward the Space Elevator.
The first resembles a winged figure, though my instruments cannot hold its shape for more than a moment. The second turns within lines of fire like a burning sword. They burn with the light of God and race through the sky like searing chariots.
I have named them Cherubim and the Lahat Ha-cherev.
Surely the Lord has sent them down here as gatekeepers of a false paradise. I foolishly attempted to pass by their contempous gaze, but God sees all.
Leah, I hope someone found you.
I hope they gave you a life beyond mine, and a name that belonged to you. I hope you were raised by people who loved you without asking you to carry their grief, their faith, or their failures. I hope that when you looked toward the future, you saw something of your own choosing rather than the ruins of what I had planned for you.
I hope you laughed every day. I hope you were stubborn like Rebecca. I hope you were kinder than I became. I hope you found love in this world, children of your own, and a home. I hope you found the blessings of God beneath these infinite heavens.
I hope that one day you know this:
I love you, Leah.
Isaac Thomas Leicester.
entries.target:
已恢復的個人日誌
作者：萊斯特，艾薩克·托馬斯
檔案： 日誌 — 最終版
我即將死去。
我在伊甸園獨居了三十六年。
最初的幾年，我走遍了各座城市、避難所、維護隧道和轉運站。我透過所有仍能運作的緊急頻道發送訊號。
沒有人回應。我知道不會有人回應。 最後一批人類技術人員早在數世紀前便已離開伊甸園，當時其建造工作已完全交由自動化群體接手。簽署那項命令的，正是我。
我 最終定居於這個我命名為加利利的地方，修繕了一棟舊農舍，並學會了務農。 閒暇時，我便在星殼中漫遊。我穿行於空蕩的城市、機器人栽種的森林，以及人類從未見過的海岸線。這裡是永無止境的白晝，彷彿還處於上帝尚未將光與暗分開之前。
伊甸園依然美麗。
哦，上帝。
我也持續嘗試恢復通往 Penelope's Star 的星門連結。起初，我告訴自己，我是為了拯救我的女兒。 如今我承認，我只是想知道是否是我親手殺了她。
哦，我的女兒。
蕾貝卡原本想給你取名叫莉亞。
致莉亞，我那從未見過面的美麗女兒：
我曾說，我是為了我深信能建構的未來而將你保存下來。這話只說對了一半。
每位醫師都告訴我，你可以被復活。 每份報告都指出你的保存艙狀況良好。但每當我想象下令解凍時，眼前便浮現蕾貝卡在復甦台上死去的身影。我讓你一直沉睡著，只因我害怕。
我將那份恐懼包裝成責任，並追逐著我那傲慢的夢想跨越了幾個世紀。 後來，當世界未能成為我所設想的模樣時，我便將你棄置於命運之中。
無論是你，還是上帝，都不欠我任何寬恕。
我每天都為你祈禱。 我為蕾貝卡祈禱。我為亡者祈禱，也為那些我從未知曉姓名、卻已將其判處死刑的生者祈禱。
我不知道上帝是否聽見了我的祈禱。
直到今天。
今天，上帝終於給出了回應。
這道通道並未連通 Penelope's Star，也非我所知的任何其他星門。 取而代之的是，兩位天使穿過地球降臨，並開始朝著太空電梯升起。
第一位形似有翼之姿，儘管我的儀器無法將其形貌捕捉超過一瞬間。 第二位則在火線之中盤旋，宛如一把燃燒的寶劍。他們熾燃著上帝之光，如灼熱的戰車般疾馳於天際。
我將他們命名為 Cherubim 與拉哈特·哈-切雷夫。
主必定是將他們派來此地，作為這虛假樂園的守門人。 我愚蠢地試圖從牠們蔑視的目光旁經過，但上帝無所不見。
莉亞，我希望有人找到了你。
我希望他們賦予你比我更美好的生命，以及屬於你自己的名字。 我希望你是由愛你的人撫養長大，他們不會要求你承擔他們的悲傷、信仰或失敗。我希望當你展望未來時，你會看到自己選擇的道路，而非我為你規劃的那片廢墟。
我希望你每天都能開懷大笑。 我希望你像蕾貝卡那樣倔強。我希望你比我後來變得更仁慈。我希望你能在這個世界上找到愛、擁有自己的孩子，以及一個家。 我希望你能在這無垠的蒼穹之下，尋得上帝的恩典。
我希望有一天你能明白這一點：
我愛你，莉亞。
艾薩克·托馬斯·萊斯特。

Restored Personal Log
Author: Lester, Isaac Thomas
File: Log — Final Version
I am about to die.
I have lived alone in Eden for thirty-six years.
In the early years, I traveled through every city, shelter, maintenance tunnel, and transit station. I sent out signals through every emergency channel that was still operational.
No one responded, I knew no one would respond. The last human technicians had left Eden centuries ago, when construction work had been fully handed over to automated systems. It was I who signed that order.
I I eventually settled in this place I named Galilee, renovated an old farmhouse, and learned to farm. In my spare time, I wander through the Star Shell. I wandered through deserted cities, robot-planted forests, and coastlines that humans had never seen. Here, the day is endless, as if we were still in the time before God had separated light from darkness.
Eden is still beautiful.
Oh, God.
I also kept trying to restore the stargate connection to Penelope’s Star. At first, I told myself I was doing it to save my daughter. Now I admit that I just want to know if I killed her with my own hands.
Oh, my daughter.
Rebecca had wanted to name you Leah.
To Leia, my beautiful daughter whom I never met:
I once said that I preserved you for the future I was convinced I could build. That was only half true.
Every doctor told me you could be revived. Every report indicated that your cryogenic chamber was in good condition. But whenever I imagined giving the order to thaw you, the image of Rebecca dying on the resuscitation table would flash before my eyes. I kept you in a deep sleep simply because I was afraid.
I disguised that fear as a sense of duty and pursued my arrogant dream across the centuries. Later, when the world failed to turn out as I had envisioned, I abandoned you to fate.
Neither you nor God owes me any forgiveness.
I pray for you every day. I pray for Rebecca. I pray for the dead, and I pray for the living—those whose names I’ve never known, yet whom I’ve already condemned to death.
I don’t know if God has heard my prayers.
Until today.
Today, God finally answered.
This passage does not lead to the Star of Penelope, nor to any other stargate I know of. Instead, two angels descended through the Earth and began ascending toward the space elevator.
The first took the form of a winged being, though my instruments could not capture its appearance for more than a fleeting moment. The second soared amidst the flames, like a blazing sword. They blazed with the Light of God, racing across the sky like a fiery chariot.
I named them Cherubim and Rahat Ha-Cheref.
The Lord must have sent them here to serve as gatekeepers of this false paradise. Foolishly, I tried to slip past their scornful gazes, but God sees all.
Leia, I hope someone has found you.
I hope they give you a life better than mine, and a name of your own. I hope you’re raised by people who love you—people who won’t burden you with their sorrow, their beliefs, or their failures. I hope that when you look to the future, you’ll see the path you’ve chosen for yourself, rather than the ruins I mapped out for you.
I hope you laugh heartily every day. I hope you are as stubborn as Rebecca. I hope you grow to be kinder than I eventually became. I hope you find love in this world, have children of your own, and build a home. I hope you find God's grace beneath this boundless sky.
I hope that one day you’ll understand this:
I love you, Leah.
Isaac Thomas Lester.

[Recovered Log — Final.]
[Filed under Gan Eden Archives in Intel.]
The elevator observation deck looks out across the impossible inward horizon. Isa says nothing for a long time.
Then she begins telling Isaac Thomas Leicester about the Shattered Ring: the wreck-farms, the revival ward, the terrible food, and every impossible ship that carried her farther than he could have imagined.
She tells him about the people who raised her, and the people she raised in turn. She tells him about her company and friends and the people that have woven themselves into her life.
She tells her about you. How you took her in. Raised her to the stars. How you gave her a new home, a new family, a new future.
No answer comes from the empty world. This time, she does not seem to need one.
entries.target:
最終日誌結束。
[已恢復日誌 — 最終篇。]
[歸檔於伊甸園檔案庫的情報分類下。]
電梯觀景台俯瞰著那道不可思議的內向地平線。 艾薩沉默了許久。
隨後，她開始向艾薩克·托馬斯·萊斯特講述破碎之環：那些殘骸農場、復活病房、難以下嚥的食物，以及每一艘載著她前往他難以想像之遠處的不可思議飛船。
她向他講述撫養她長大的人們，以及她後來撫養的人們。她向他講述她的夥伴、朋友，以及那些已融入她生命中的人們。
她向他講述關於你的事。 你如何收留了她。將她撫育至璀璨如星。你如何賦予她一個新家、一個新家庭、一個嶄新的未來。
空蕩的世界沒有任何回應。這次，她似乎也不需要任何回應。
entries.backTranslation:
End of Final Log.
[Log Restored — Final Entry.]
[Archived under the Intelligence category in the Eden Archives.]
The elevator observation deck overlooked that incredible inward-curving horizon. Isaac remained silent for a long time.
Then she began to tell Isaac Thomas Lester about the Broken Ring: the wreck farms, the resuscitation wards, the unpalatable food, and every incredible spaceship that had carried her to places he could never imagine.
She told him about the people who raised her, and the people she later raised. She told him about her companions, her friends, and those who had become a part of her life.
She told him about you. How you took her in. How you nurtured her until she shone as brightly as a star. How you gave her a new home, a new family, and a brand-new future.
The empty world offered no response. This time, it seemed she didn’t need one either.

You find her pressed face-first against the glass of an observation blister, watching Hegemony-pattern ships parade one by one down a parallel departure queue. Her slate displays a hologram of each passing vessel, all of them carefully logged and annotated.
"Look at that armor profile," she says without turning. "Every Hegemony ship looks like it expects the universe to sucker-punch it, so it makes sure to swing first. Strike hard, strike true, strike only once." She nods approvingly. "Decisive Battle Doctrine."
You nod toward the security overhang crowning the docks.

entries.source:
After your fleet enters $marketName's docking queue, you exit the ship. You find Isa standing among a crowd of spectators, staring up at the star-filled sky.
A local League detachment is putting on an in-atmosphere airshow. Flights of G-10 Thunders scream overhead to delighted cheers, banking between the station's towers before scattering into precise, independent formations.
Isa, however, is silent.
A Thunder makes a particularly low pass over the concourse. Its exhaust washes through the crowd, sending coats, hats, and unsecured market displays fluttering in its wake. Isa's hair sweeps across her eyes, but her gaze never wavers. She watches the fighters climb away, one by one, before disappearing into the waiting bays of their Heron carrier.
"Look at them," she says quietly. "The stats say most fighter pilots have a life expectancy measured in hours after first contact. It's a job for suicidal people, honestly."
Her slate lights up with a purchase listing for a surplus Thunder wing.
"But for a few minutes at a time, they're the only people in the fleet who get to choose exactly where they go."
She opens the technical specifications.
"I think I understand the appeal."

一架雷霆戰機以極低高度掠過大廳。尾流席捲人群，吹得外套、帽子和未固定的市場展品四處翻飛。艾薩的頭髮掃過眼睛，她的目光卻沒有動搖。她看著戰機一架接一架爬升，最後消失在蒼鷺號航母敞開的機庫中。

entries.source:
The next time you find her, she is standing before the panoramic window of a Tri-Tachyon show berth. Beyond the glass, an Afflictor-class frigate hangs motionless against the stars, its hull picked out by cold blue running lights.
A pleasant synthetic voice fills the concourse.
"Observe the elegance of total battlespace control."
The Afflictor vanishes.
A heartbeat later, it reappears several kilometers away, directly behind a target drone. The drone comes apart under a burst of laser fire. Polite applause ripples through the showroom.
Isa leans toward the glass.
"...Turn rate and speed were far too high for secondary thrusters, and I don't see any extra exhaust ports," she mutters. "Did those psychopaths actually disable the safety interlocks for a marketing stunt?"
entries.target:
下次你找到她時，她正佇立在速子科技展示艙的全景窗前。玻璃窗外，一艘折磨級護衛艦靜止地懸浮於星際之間，冷藍色的行進燈光勾勒出其船體輪廓。
一陣悅耳的人工合成語音響徹大廳。
"請欣賞這無與倫比的戰場全面掌控之美。"
折磨號瞬間消失。
一瞬間後，它又在數公里外、一架目標無人機的正後方重新出現。那架無人機在激光連射下支離破碎。 展廳內響起一陣禮貌的掌聲。
艾薩俯身貼近玻璃。
"……這樣的轉向率和速度對輔助推進器來說實在太高了，而且我沒看到任何額外的排氣口，" 她低聲嘀咕道。 "那些瘋子難道真的為了行銷噱頭，而關閉了安全互鎖裝置嗎？"
entries.backTranslation:
The next time you find her, she is standing before the panoramic window of the Soku Technology exhibition pod. Beyond the glass, a Suffering-class frigate hovers motionless in interstellar space, its cold blue navigation lights outlining the contours of its hull.
A melodious synthetic voice echoed through the hall.
" Please admire the unparalleled beauty of total battlefield dominance. "
The *Sufferer* vanished in an instant.
A moment later, it reappeared several kilometers away, directly behind a target drone. The drone was torn to pieces under a barrage of laser fire. A round of polite applause rang out in the exhibition hall.
Isa leaned in close to the glass.
"……That rate of turn and speed are way too high for auxiliary thrusters, and I don’t see any extra exhaust ports, " she muttered under her breath. " Did those lunatics really disable the safety interlocks just for a marketing gimmick? "

Isa gives you a frown.
"Efficient ain't the same thing as harmless, $shipTrophyIsaPlayerTitle."
She turns the slate around. Beneath the financing offer is a projected repayment schedule extending several years beyond her estimated life expectancy.
"Though they did get my preferred reactor configuration right."
Isa begins digging through the concourse app's privacy settings. Each menu opens into three more menus, all of them already set to OPTIMAL.
"I think entering the concourse counted as consent."
She pauses.
"Possibly docking at the station counted as consent."
entries.target:
艾薩對你皺了皺眉。
"高效不等於無害，$shipTrophyIsaPlayerTitle。"
她將石板翻了過來。 融資方案下方列出的預計還款時間表，其期限甚至超出了她的預期壽命好幾年。
"雖然他們確實正確地採用了我偏好的反應爐配置。"
艾薩開始仔細檢視大廳應用程式的隱私權設定。 每個選單展開後又會出現三個子選單，而且全都預設為最佳模式。
"我想，進入中庭這件事本身就等同於同意了。"
她停頓了一下。
"或許在車站停靠本身就等同於同意。"
entries.backTranslation:
Aisa frowned at you.
" High efficiency doesn’t mean it’s harmless, $shipTrophyIsaPlayerTitle. "
She flipped the slate over. The projected repayment schedule listed below the financing plan extended several years beyond her expected lifespan.
" Although they had indeed correctly adopted my preferred reactor configuration. "
Isa began carefully reviewing the privacy settings for the lobby app. Each menu, when expanded, revealed three submenus, all of which were set to Optimal Mode by default.
" I suppose simply entering the atrium is tantamount to consent. "
She paused for a moment.
" Perhaps simply stopping at a station is tantamount to consent. "

entries.source:
Isa pulls a small data wafer from her pack and plugs it into a secondary port on her slate.
Her slate's display fractures into a hundred miniature windows, each controlled by one of her own delta-level AI agents.
Bulk agricultural machinery.
Ceremonial armor polish.
Volturnian lobster breeding equipment.
Industrial quantities of devotional candles.
On her many screens, the advertisements flicker. Sleek phase ships disappear, replaced by increasingly confused offers for farming equipment, shrine furnishings, and twelve thousand liters of crustacean feed.
Isa smiles.
"There. Now we're both learning."
Her slate vibrates again.
A complete phase-coil maintenance manual has been added to her account as a complimentary incentive.
She bookmarks it.

entries.source:
The concourse resembles a fuel depot rebuilt as an Andrada-themed amusement park. Purple neon traces the bulkheads. Animated Lions salute from every wall. Somewhere behind a museum gift shop and a Volturnian lobster petting pool, the same eight bars of techno begin again. Multiple clubs are playing the same song, at seemed.
The arrivals portal deposits you directly in Isa's path.
She nearly collides with you, arms piled high with Andrada merchandise, a curly straw clenched between her lips. It runs down into a massive, five-gallon novelty cup shaped like a Prometheus PM-15000.
Isa stops. She lowers her sunglasses, revealing another pair waiting underneath.
After a moment, she gives you a solemn nod, turns on her heel, walks right into one of your bodyguards, probably near blind due to the double-layers of shades she was wearing and marches back toward the command ship.
entries.target:
這座大廳宛如一座燃料庫，經改建後成為以 Andrada 為主題的遊樂園。紫色霓虹燈沿著艙壁延伸。動畫中的獅子從每面牆壁向你致意。在博物館禮品店和沃爾圖尼亞龍蝦觸摸池的某處後方，那段相同的八小節電子樂又重新響起。 多間夜店似乎都在播放同一首歌。
抵達傳送門將你直接送到了艾薩的行進路徑上。
她差點與你相撞，雙臂堆滿了 Andrada 的周邊商品，嘴唇間緊咬著一根捲曲的吸管。 吸管一直伸進一個巨大的五加侖造型紀念杯裡，杯身做成普羅米修斯 PM-15000.
艾薩停下腳步。 她拉下太陽眼鏡，露出底下還藏著的另一副眼鏡。
片刻後，她向你鄭重地點了點頭，隨即轉身，直接撞上你的其中一名保鑣——那人大概因為她戴著雙層太陽眼鏡而幾乎看不見——然後大步朝指揮艦走去。

entries.source:
Before clearing customs, you pass through a visitors' concourse glowing with Andradan restaurants, jewelers, and imported food.
The lights end at the customs barrier.
On the other side, you find Isa chatting with a couple of Diktat engineers beside the arrivals portal. She waves, breaks off from the conversation, and joins you.
There are no shops here. Only state dispensaries, shuttered offices, and a Diktat commissar standing on a raised pulpit, holding a portrait of Andrada above a line of workers.
"By the Lion's mercy," he announces, "every loyal citizen eats. Andrada sees your glorious labor and smiles upon you!"
Through a tiny window, a clerk hands each laborer a foil-wrapped ration small enough to palm. On one of the ration packets, the Diktat emblem has been stamped slightly off-center. Beneath it, part of a Hegemony logo remains visible.
HEGAID.
Isa watches a shipforge worker tuck his ration under one arm and shuffle away. You can hear the commissar repeat his propaganda, over and over, like a chant.
"$shipTrophyIsaPlayerTitle."
entries.target:
在通過海關之前，你會經過一座訪客大廳，那裡有Andrada 式餐廳、珠寶店和進口食品，整片區域光芒四射。
燈光在海關閘口處戛然而止。
在閘口另一側，你發現艾薩正與幾位辛達強權工程師在抵達通道旁閒聊。 她向你揮手，結束對話，並走向你。
這裡沒有商店。只有國營藥房、拉下卷簾門的辦公室，以及一位站在高台上的辛達強權政治委員，他手持 Andrada 的肖像，俯視著一排工人。

entries.backTranslation:
Before passing through customs, you will walk through a visitor hall featuring the Andradan Restaurant, a jewelry store, and imported foods—the entire area is aglow.
The lights come to an abrupt halt at the customs gate.
On the other side of the gate, you find Isa chatting with several Dictat engineers beside the arrival corridor. She waves to you, ends the conversation, and walks toward you.
There are no shops here. Only a state-run pharmacy, offices with their shutters down, and a Dictat political commissar standing on a raised platform, holding a portrait of Andrada and looking down on a line of workers.
" By the grace of the Lion King, " he proclaimed, " every loyal citizen will have enough to eat. Andrada bears witness to your glorious labor and smiles down upon you! "
Through a small window, a clerk hands each worker a ration wrapped in tin foil—small enough to fit in the palm of one’s hand. On one of the ration packets, the Dictat emblem was stamped slightly off-center. Below it, part of the Hegemony’s emblem was still faintly visible.
HEGAID.
Isa watched as a shipyard worker tucked the ration under his arm and walked away. You could hear the political commissar repeating his propaganda lines over and over, as if reciting a poem.
"$shipTrophyIsaPlayerTitle."

You leave the arrivals portal behind.
The station's traffic-control feed is crowded with Diktat hulls, every one polished for inspection. On the main display, a parade fleet of Lion's Guard ships-the supposed elite of Philip Andrada's navy.
Finally perking up, Isa zooms in on an Executor until its gilded weapon housings fill the display.
"Look at the placement of those ordnance mounts," she says. "Ballistics forward for shield suppression. Energy weapons held back for armor and hull."
She studies the altered mounts, then brings up the specifications for its Lion's Guard escorts.
"What went wrong...?"
entries.target:
你將抵達傳送門拋在身後。
空間站的交通管制畫面中擠滿了辛達強權艦體，每一艘都經過拋光以備檢查。 主螢幕上，一隊獅心衛隊艦船正列隊遊行——號稱是 Philip Andrada 海軍的菁英。
艾薩終於精神一振，將鏡頭拉近一艘執行官級戰艦，直到其鍍金的武器艙體填滿整個螢幕。
"看看那些武器架的配置，"她說道。"前部配置彈道武器用於壓制護盾，後部配置能量武器用於攻擊裝甲與船體。"
她仔細研究了這些經過改裝的武器架，接著調出其獅心衛隊護航艦的規格資料。
"到底出了什麼問題……？"
entries.backTranslation:
You'll arrive with the teleportation gate behind you. The traffic control screen of the
space station is filled with Dictator-class vessels, each polished to a shine in preparation for inspection. On the main screen, a squadron of Lion Guard ships is parading in formation—reportedly the elite of the Philip Andrada Navy.
Aisa finally perked up and zoomed in on an Executor-class battleship until its gilded weapon bays filled the entire screen.
" Look at the configuration of those weapon mounts, " she said. " Ballistic weapons are mounted at the front to suppress shields, while energy weapons are mounted at the rear to attack armor and the hull. "
She carefully studied these modified weapon mounts, then pulled up the specifications for her Lion Guard escort ship.
" What on earth is going on…? "

Isa lowers her slate and sighs.

" To be honest, the Enforcer is truly impressive. Its escort ships, on the other hand, are absolute junk. "

Isa set down her logpad and sighed.
" I'm heading back to the fleet. "

A young Pather mechanic notices Isa studying an exposed power junction.
"You know reactors, sister?"
His voice is friendly. He offers her a cup of tea from the flask beside his tools.
Isa accepts it cautiously.
"A little."
He shows her a schematic and asks how to keep an overloaded core from shutting itself down. Isa begins to answer.

"You aren't trying to save this ship."
The mechanic smiles.
"No, sister."

這時她注意到反應堆示意圖下方標有民用應答器代碼。

The doors of a dockside bar slam open.
A pirate stumbles into the concourse, wild-eyed.
"I'll pay! I swear I'll pay this time!"
Several others emerge behind him. They seize him by the arms and legs, carry him to the edge of the dock, and throw him screaming and pleading through the grav field.
He hangs outside the station without a helmet, kicking soundlessly against the stars. His eyes bulge and his face begins to swell. Every desperate jerks sends the breath leaking from his lungs, turning him end over end, helplessly in the void.
After ten seconds, they drag him back by a tether around his ankle.
The moment he crosses the railing, he collapses onto the deck, wheezing and coughing blood while the bar erupts in laughter.

Isa is frowning, manipulating a diagram of a ship with abrupt flicks at the interface. "It'd have to be anchored to the flux grid. Only way to keep it wrapped close enough to the hull geometry."
"Precisely," Tech says. "To keep the exotic material from diminishing! It will draw energy from incoming projectiles, storing it in the, um... meta-plasma?"
Isa snorts dismissively.
"Merely a working term," Tech says defensively.

艾薩正皺著眉頭，在介面上以急促的指尖滑動操作著一艘飛船的示意圖。"它必須錨定在磁通網格上。 這是讓它緊貼船體幾何結構的唯一方法。"
"正是如此，" 技術部門說道。 "這樣才能防止那種奇異物質耗損！它會從飛來的彈丸中汲取能量，並將其儲存於……呃……超等離子體中？"
艾薩不屑地哼了一聲。
"這只是個工作術語罷了，" 技術人員辯解道。

Aisa frowned as she swiped her finger rapidly across the interface, navigating a schematic of a spaceship. " It must be anchored to the magnetic flux grid. That’s the only way to keep it aligned with the ship’s geometry. "
" Exactly, said the technical department. " That’s the only way to prevent that strange material from being depleted! It draws energy from incoming projectiles and stores it in… uh… a superplasma? "
Isa snorted dismissively.
" It’s just a technical term, " the technician explained.
